You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Additional demos: a 9 diagonal ray continued along the diagonal; a vertical 6 pair and a nonmatching mixed-color pattern were unchanged.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:49:54.640067+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T02:49:54.640084+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_tile_four_rotations_into_a_2x2_block', kind='memory', title='ARC tile four rotations into a 2x2 block', content='For this ARC task family, enlarge an n×n grid to 2n×2n by placing four orientations of the input in a 2×2 arrangement: top-left = original; top-right = 90° clockwise rotation; bottom-left = 90° counterclockwise rotation; bottom-right = 180° rotation. This is useful for ARC tasks where an incomplete outline/line drawing encodes missing cells.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T07:11:15.545291+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T07:11:15.545307+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_extend_diagonal_duplicate_color_rays_away_from_marker', kind='memory', title='ARC extend diagonal duplicate-color rays away from marker', content='For ARC grids with a small motif containing two adjacent same-color diagonal pairs (each repeated color appears in two cells stepping one row down and one column left/right) plus one or more marker-colored cell(s) on the opposite side, extend each repeated-color diagonal as a ray from the pair, continuing away from the marker arrangement until the grid edge.
